top3.t: Nasdaq -2.60% and S&P 500 -1.21% Thursday; Lam Research -11.8%, Nvidia -4.4%.
Tadawul -2.3%, an eighth straight weekly fall; SNB -5.1% as Houthi attacks hit.
Brent +4.00% to USD 113.17 as the Iran war and Gulf attacks threaten supply.

cotd.name: Moderna
cotd.body: Moderna (Nasdaq: MRNA), the US maker of mRNA medicines, closed Thursday at USD 202.63 (-17.6% from USD 245.81) and fell as much as 25% intraday when full results of its melanoma vaccine, developed with Merck, leaked online before release. With Merck's drug Keytruda, it cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% in a 1,100-patient trial. Merck closed -1.8% at USD 147.24.

cotd.chart_title: Moderna is +657.8% in 12 months despite -17.6% on 22.10
cotd.chart_method: Weekly closes from 24.10.2025, then daily closes to 22.10.2026 (official), rebased to 100.
cotd.catalyst: Two-year melanoma data are due at the ESMO cancer congress in Madrid on Saturday 24.10.
cotd.means: No direct Gulf link; for a dollar-based Gulf portfolio it shows the one-day risk in a stock that had risen 658% in 12 months.

left: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy said it hit four vessels in illegal oil transfers in the northern Gulf on Wednesday.
The implied chance of a December Fed hike fell to 85%, no longer fully priced.
France's benchmark bond yield rose to about 5.04%, its highest since July 2002; its gap over German Bunds is 163 basis points.
right: US 10-year 4.96% (-17 bp), 2-year 4.65% (-16 bp), 30-year 5.29% (-13 bp) as investors bought bonds.
Meta closed at USD 648.85 (-7.0%) a day after results, on its first cash outflow in over a decade.
Procter & Gamble closed +5.6% at USD 165.59 after beating profit forecasts; rail operator CSX rose 6.8% to USD 51.67 on a profit beat.

extras_left.label: Number of the day
extras_left.text: Six big Saudi banks' Q3 profit, up 5.3% year on year

extras_right.label: Coming up
extras_right.text: Sat 24.10: Moderna and Merck present two-year data at ESMO in Madrid; Tadawul reopens Sunday.

gcc_panels.caption: These lenders hold about SAR 2.5 tn of loans; AlJazira grew fastest.

left: SNB, the Kingdom's largest lender, fell 5.1% Thursday, Emirates NBD 2.9% and Qatar National Bank 1.0%.
Egypt's main index fell 3.4% to 51,052, its biggest intraday drop since June 2025.
After a new Houthi wave, Riyadh struck missile-launcher sites and said it intercepted many ballistic missiles.
Saudi Kayan, a SABIC-affiliated petrochemical maker, lost SAR 94.2 m in Q3 against SAR 336.3 m a year earlier.
Aramco plans to double overseas crude storage and seeks foreign strategic reserves; its Red Sea pipeline target is 10 m barrels a day, up from 7 m.
right: Front-month futures Thursday: Brent USD 113.17 (+4.00%, +85.98% YTD), WTI USD 99.47 (+2.39%, +73.23% YTD); Brent traded higher in Asia on Friday.
Gold USD 4,060.40 (-2.16%, -6.47% YTD) with no safe-haven bid; dollar index 101.61 (-0.17%, +3.39% YTD).
Lam Research, the chipmaking-equipment maker, closed at USD 230.15 (-11.8%) despite beating forecasts, as its profit guidance midpoint came in slightly lower.
Nvidia, the largest US stock, closed -4.4% at USD 212.21 and CoreWeave, the AI cloud group, -10.1% at USD 55.60 on debt worries.
The CSI 300 closed Thursday at 4,036.30 (-1.84%, -12.82% YTD) and lost 1.1% more on Friday, its lowest since July 2025.

watch.label: The question this week
watch.text: Does the US 10-year yield stay under 5% (4.96% on 22.10) into the Fed meeting on 27-28.10, with a December hike still about 85% priced?
